items.stem: Why does a container typically start faster and use fewer resources than a full virtual machine?

options.text: It shares the host kernel instead of booting its own
options.rationale: Correct: containers run as isolated processes sharing the host kernel, avoiding a full OS boot.

options.text: It compresses the application into a single CPU instruction
options.rationale: Containers do not reduce an app to one instruction; that is not how they work.

options.text: It runs only on read-only hardware
options.rationale: Hardware mode is unrelated to container startup speed.
Containers use memory; they simply avoid a separate guest OS.

items.explanation: Correct: containers run as isolated processes sharing the host kernel, avoiding a full OS boot.

items.stem: A database container loses all its records every time it is recreated. Which change fixes this?

options.text: Attach a persistent volume for the database data directory
options.rationale: Correct: a volume stores data outside the container's writable layer so it survives recreation.

options.text: Add more CPU to the container
options.rationale: CPU allocation does not affect data persistence.

options.text: Rename the container on each run
options.rationale: The name does not preserve the writable layer's data.
Ports affect network access, not data durability.

items.explanation: Correct: a volume stores data outside the container's writable layer so it survives recreation.

items.stem: Select TWO practices that reduce the final size of a container image.

options.rationale: Correct: a smaller base image means fewer bytes in every build.

options.text: Combining and cleaning up package installs in fewer layers
options.rationale: Correct: removing caches within the same layer keeps them out of the final image.

options.text: Copying the entire project including build artifacts and caches
options.rationale: Copying unneeded files inflates the image.

options.text: Adding every optional tool 'just in case'
options.rationale: Unused tools only increase size and attack surface.

items.explanation: Correct: a smaller base image means fewer bytes in every build. Correct: removing caches within the same layer keeps them out of the final image.
